text_fidelity_a:
Lowepro LP36915 ViewPoint CS 40 - A Soft-Sided Protective Case for a Smartphone, GoPro or 360 Camera and Accessories,Black The good:

Its slim profile. But it will still hold a lot of gear.

The case within the backpack that slides in and out the side hatch, with positionable dividers. Just right for GoPro or sports type cameras.

The laptop section. My laptop measures 10 by 15 inches and an inch thick. It fits like the pack was made for it. I doubt any larger laptop would fit. The laptop section is right on the back, but there is padding to keep things comfortable.

The shoulder straps are comfortable and very adjustable.

The designed places for headphones and small tripods/monopods and batteries and other various gear.

The expandable pocket on the side opposite the inner case hatch.

It has several straps to grab and carry the pack or stow extra items.

It's well made, with even stitching throughout.

The not-so-good:

The waist strap is a sufficient length. But the chest strap is way too short. A teenager would have trouble fastening it. That's a bit of a concern if you're bombing down a hill on a bike and only one of the two front straps is long enough to latch. It kind of compromises the security.

It's not versatile. It's a little too small for DSLRs or bridge cameras. If the slide-in case and backpack were just an inch or so deeper it would hold them. That's not really a flaw though since this was designed for GoPro or sports type cameras and gear.

I think there was a missed opportunity to put an expandable pocket or two on the front. The pockets there will only hold flat materials. But that does keep the profile neat and slim.

Overall it's a really good pack, but maybe could be a smidgen better.
text_fidelity_b: Lowepro LP36915 ViewPoint CS 40 - A Soft-Sided Protective Case for a Smartphone, GoPro or 360 Camera and Accessories,Black

text_fidelity_a:
Kodak DC3400 2MP Digital Camera with 2x Optical Zoom I'm just an amateur when it comes to photography. All I really want is an easy-to-use point-and-shoot camera that I can take on vacations to snap shots of places I find interesting, to use around the house to take photos of valuables for insurance purposes, etc. In other words, my expectations are pretty minimal.
That said, I'm extremely happy with the Kodak DC3400. This is my second Kodak digital (my first was a DC240), so obviously I'm pleased with the Kodak product line.
After unpacking the DC3400, I spent about 10 minutes getting it set up, and proceeded to take a few pictures. Another 10 minutes or so, and I had the photo software loaded on my laptop. Connect the USB cable, and I was able to load the photos onto the laptop immediately. The camera shows up as an icon, like a disk drive, which you can double-click to open and transfer the pictures to a folder on your hard drive -- piece of cake!
The quality of the pictures is amazing. I use the Ofoto service, and had some prints of some of my digital photos sent to my mother. According to her, you could not tell the difference between the digital images and those taken with a 35mm film camera. The colors were vivid, the images sharp -- just what you'd expect from the Kodak name.
I'll agree with most everyone else and say that batteries might be the only downside to this camera. It's definitely worth the investment to get the Kodak NiMh rechargables and the charger. The ONLY time I use NiCads is when I'm my NiMh set is in the recharger, and I need to snap a few pictures.
For the money, I don't think you can top this camera in terms of features, quality, and ease of use.
text_fidelity_b: Kodak DC3400 2MP Digital Camera with 2x Optical Zoom

text_fidelity_a:
RCA RD1006 Discwasher D4+ Vinyl Record Care System This is the best record cleaning I tried so far. I is very effective in removing dust (and associated static noise) from records that are in reasonably good shape. Of course, it cannot repair records which have been damaged due to being played while dirty. If you acquire a used record in dirty condition, it is probably a good idea to wash it with distilled water first before using the discwasher on it.

I noticed that there are several one-star reviews complaining about the direction of fibers on the cleaning pad that comes with this system. Yes, the cords of the corduroy-like microfiber material does run along the edge of the brush, but this is actually how it should be to provide even coverage across all the grooves. The cords of any fabric is much too thick to fit into the actual grooves on the record. If the cords were to run along the direction of the the grooves, some grooves would be cleaned and some wouldn't. Having the cords being perpendicular to the grooves on the record ensures that all grooves get cleaned evenly. After all, it is the microfibers, not the cords of the fabric, doing the cleaning.

Another advantage of cords running perpendicular to the grooves of the record is that, as you slowly rotate the brush on its axis (as shown in the provided directions), dust that has been collected gets trapped between the cords that are being lifted off the record as the next (clean) cord of the fabric starts making contact with the record surface.
text_fidelity_b: RCA RD1006 Discwasher D4+ Vinyl Record Care System

text_fidelity_a:
TCL 65" Class 4-Series 4K UHD HDR Roku 2017 Smart TV - 65S405 Was hesitant to buy a not so known brand. However for the most part its a really good TV. Did some research on TCL and found out that several tv brands were in fact manufactered by TCL. Emerson, RCA, Phillips etc.

I did pay extra for a entended warranty because the last 2 tv's I owned both went to the recycle bin in about 2.5 years. However, the extended warranty for parts and labor worked out to be about 10$ a year. The Insurance company figures that the failure rate isnt going to be that significant based on how low the cost for the warranty.

The remote and the menus on the TV dont have much functionality. I guess Roku thought that having a more plug and play approach would be better. The app for your mobile device has that functionality though. Can change picture settings etc. I have yet to find the sound options though. Be aware that going to external speakers via audio out also cuts off the internal speakers. Picture quality is really good overall. There are times though that it appears to be trying to upconvert to the 4K from a lower definition video stream and when it does there are some interesting visual artifacts. I don't know why but I think that some streaming services have encoded the audio of their content differently due to needing to increase volume on TV from say 35 to 95 in order to hear it. As a example Netflix volume on tv 35 to 40.. Amazon prime I have to increase volume to 90 or higher to achieve same level of hearing as Netflix. There are variations of course but generally speaking over the entirety of the video libraries of both services thats what I have to do. Blue ray is fantastic through TV.

I do have several years experience with roku streaming devices and those do work well and I have never had a hardware failure in them. I would suggest setting up a roku account before initializing TV. Makes setup way easier.

Havent been able to notice a difference between wired connection and wired as far as visually or sonically.

Overall, for a 55 inch class TV for the price.. Decent deal. Will have to see how the hardware lasts.
text_fidelity_b: TCL 65" Class 4-Series 4K UHD HDR Roku 2017 Smart TV - 65S405

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Wireless Rechargeable Laser Mouse 7000 Mac/Windows I have mixed feelings about this mouse. On one hand it is a pleasure to use. On the other, charging it leaves much to be desired.

This is a fairly large mouse, sculpted nicely to fit most peoples' hands. I have large hands and I have found this mouse to be a good fit. It is comfortable to grip, the scroll wheel is smooth and easy to turn, and the buttons are easy to press without being hyper-sensitive. Ergonomics are this mouse's strongest attribute.

In use, the mouse is on par with other Microsoft mice I have used. It is accurate. Unlike some of the comments by other reviewers here, I have had no issue with it being too sensitive or too precise. The performance has, in my opinion, been average. This is not a bad thing - Microsoft mice are usually very consistent and this one fits the norm.

Where I ran into difficulty with this mouse was in charging it. I read a lot of other reviews on this mouse beforehand so I was prepared for issues with charging. That said, I was still having issues getting the mouse to charge the battery until I cut part of a 3x5 index card, folded it up and crammed it into the battery compartment with the battery. There have been enough other people that have had to do similarly odd things to rule out the possibility of this being an isolated case.

The battery can be put into a normal charger, but that defeats the purpose.

This is not a bad mouse. It's actually quite good and I would recommend it except for the recharging issue. As a wireless mouse it is fine, but as a recharging mouse it needs a design revisit.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Wireless Rechargeable Laser Mouse 7000 Mac/Windows

Anker Soundcore Bluetooth Speaker with 24-Hour Playtime, 66-Feet Bluetooth Range & Built-in Mic, Dual-Driver Portable Wireless Speaker with Low Harmonic Distortion and Superior Sound - Blue I own the A3143 Premium Stereo Bluetooth speaker (2x10W=20W) which sounds great, but it doesn't have a microphone or the longer battery life of this lower-cost A3102 SoundCore speaker (2x3W=6W). The features and sound characteristics are different, but which is the better choice depends on personal preference. To me based on sound quality alone, the A3143 wins hands down. The bass is stronger (more power is required to drive the lower frequencies than the higher frequencies), but I also find overall frequency response to be more balanced and accurate for instruments and vocals. For either speaker, I'd recommend using an EQ app to set the frequency response and spatial effects to your preference (I use Bass EQ from Coocent). Interestingly, the maximum volume level for both the A3143 and this A3102 SoundCore are about the same.

The A3102 has a brighter sound overall. The A3102 is good as a general purpose speaker, and it is excellent to use with a cell phone. The A3102 microphone (which the A3143 doesn't have) and speaker quality for voice calling are crisp and clear. My dad who can't hear very well often could not understand me on my cell phone handset or its speakerphone, but had no problem when I used the A3102.

So for long battery life, good overall music speaker, and particularly for use as a microphone/speakerphone for voice calls, A3102 is a good choice. For best music reproduction, the A3143. For either, Anker's quality and customer support are among the best in the industry.
text_fidelity_b: Anker Soundcore Bluetooth Speaker with 24-Hour Playtime, 66-Feet Bluetooth Range & Built-in Mic, Dual-Driver Portable Wireless Speaker with Low Harmonic Distortion and Superior Sound - Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Xit XTETS Auto Focus Macro Extension Tube Set for Sony SLR Cameras (Black) UPDATE: I have since bought a couple of other cheap extension tube sets that looked similar. As it turns out, this set is actually very good for a crappy tube set. They all seem to cheap out on the electrical connections, so, especially when you're linking more than one tube, they can loose the auto signals and the camera may give you an error. But these work enough of the time to be useful. ALSO IMPORTANT: These are better for internal reflections than most. They have nice masks (baffles) in the tubes and have shiny bits hidden. That's crucial for good macro. Otherwise you will have hazy photos. SO I UPGRADED the rating from my original review below.
NOT ALL OF THESE TUBES THAT LOOK SIMILAR ARE THE SAME!

If you're using these for professional work, buy Canon tubes (or Kenko are supposed to be good).

ORIGINAL REVIEW
These tubes are sold under many names (The flippy metal release tabs and the smallest tube being 13mm instead of 12mm are a tip off).

I didn't really think the quality of extension tubes mattered. They're hollow tubes with some wires running through them for electrical contacts! Hard to mess up. But this set (at least the one I received) is messed up.

Sometimes my camera (Canon 70D) will just throw up an error when these are attached. Often just after snapping the shutter.

NEVER did autofocus work.

NEVER would more than one tube hold on to the connection to the camera long enough to give an exposure without an error.

I did manage to get some photos with auto exposure working, but always with manual focus. I don't think the image stabilizer was working either (from all the shaking). I didn't test it by switching it off.

The mounts are plastic, but not the kind you get on a cheap lens. More like the kind you get on a cheap kids toy with fake chrome. NOT smooth. You get a sort of sandpapery feel when you turn it into the mount.

I'm throwing mine away. I won't pay up for Canon's tubes (at that price - I'd buy the macro lens first), but there has to be something better than this.
text_fidelity_b: Xit XTETS Auto Focus Macro Extension Tube Set for Sony SLR Cameras (Black)

I'd used MSI several times in the past, and was happy with their product quality and their support. (BTW, I use pcpartpicker to assemble my components, I recommend the site.)

For the price paid, the value of this mobo is excellent. I highly recommend considering it for a mid-priced Ryzen build.

text_fidelity_a:
Nulaxy Bluetooth Car FM Transmitter Audio Adapter Receiver Wireless Handsfree Voltmeter Car Kit TF Card AUX 1.44 Display – KM18 Peacock Blue *UPDATED REVIEW*

A seller replaced a different defective FM transmitter unit with this one for me (mine has the Kollea brand name on it, but this is the identical unit, private-labeled). This is a better product than what it replaced, but is not without it's flaws. I have three (*UPDATE: now four, and the fourth one is a deal-breaker--see below) complaints with this unit:

1) It will not automatically reconnect to my phone about 75% of the time. I have to manually shut Bluetooth off and turn it back on on the phone, sometimes a few times before it pairs successfully. This is a hassle--a PITA. Every time I get in the car, I have to go through this process--every time power is cut from the transmitter, actually, so if your passenger knocks it and it pops out of the 12V socket, it will have to be re-paired, which is supposed to happen automatically, but does not, and you then have to go through the process. Frustrating.

2) Charge output is only 1.0A. this is why I returned the first one--phone gives a "slow charging" warning when charging from this unit, regardless of what USB cable I use (I tried four different cables, all of which I know for certain can carry 2.1A).

3) Callers have occasionally complained they cannot hear me well when using this unit, and I occasionally (but not often) encounter FM interference. I believe Bluetooth itself is part of the problem, and anyone who has used a few Bluetooth headsets or units like this knows audio quality is terrible. Period. We just deal with it. Add to that the burden of having to transmit your signal via FM to a car stereo and the user-side audio (what you will hear in your car) is always going to be craptastic.

4) (*UPDATE) When paired, voice recognition on my phone, which is usually quite good, becomes severely impaired. This is also likely the culprit for complaint #3, above. I suspect this is because when paired, it tries to use the built-in microphone for voice recognition instead of the microphones on my phone (of which there are 4). It is disabling the extremely good microphones in my phone (Nokia lumia Icon which is well known for having incredible audio input) and using the unit's crappy microphone instead. This microphone is located in the unit, which is attached to the center console of my car near the shifter, and thus picks up all the vibrations and related road and engine noise transmitted through the structure of the car as I drive. This approach is terrible. I have stopped using the unit for anything requiring voice input, including telephone calls. In other words, this is just a big awkward charger now, and one that charges painfully slowly (see complaint #2). If it were possible to disable the onboard mic, and use the mics in my phone instead for calls and voice recognition, this would be a much more serviceable unit As it is now, it is just a piece of junk.

Cannot recommend this item. There are definitely worse products out there. I have not tried them all, but of those I have used, this is the best one so far. I will likely keep using it until the lack of automatic pairing pushes me over the edge with it one day and I get something else. (*UPDATE: this thing just does not work well, and I am now looking for something else.)
text_fidelity_b: Nulaxy Bluetooth Car FM Transmitter Audio Adapter Receiver Wireless Handsfree Voltmeter Car Kit TF Card AUX 1.44 Display – KM18 Peacock Blue

Wall Outlet Extender Surge Protector - 6 Outlet Wall Adapter with 3 USB Charging Ports (1 USB-C, 2 USB A), Multi Plug Outlets Wall Mount with Top Phone Holder for Home, Dorm Essentail, 490 Joules There has been an unpleasant shift, from who is responsible for supplying the power adapters for USB powered appliances. And, for the number of simple household appliances that now require those adapters. I suppose that I can see the logic in it. Newer electrical devices now require lower power. Thence, adapters. At first, they came with the device, like cell phones were supplied with the wall adapters. Eventually, you had to buy your own adapters. Even now, you have to be careful in selecting an adapter. There are basic ones that only have 3 amps. Some have 5 amps or more. Some only split all their power between multiple ports. Some are 'smart' and provide all the amps needed to multiple devices. Now, that's pretty much the rule. You gotta do it yourself and you better know what you're looking for. Disappointment is more common than satisfaction, in this new game.

These outlet adapters from Mifusa probably wouldn't have been my optimum choice, had the listing been a little more informative. But, based on what I read and how it works, it will do well enough.

The six outlets are too close together for bulky plugs or those that have the transformers built into the plugs. The total amperage across all three USB ports is only 3 amps. So, don't look to power multiple USB devices efficiently. BUT, you CAN plug six AC (that's alternating current, not air conditioning) of a low enough power draw, and three USB powered devices, IF they will all fit in the MIFUSA device, and know that they also have surge protection, as indicated by the little green light.

One star being crap and five stars being spectacular, I rate these as being 'okay'.
text_fidelity_b: Wall Outlet Extender Surge Protector - 6 Outlet Wall Adapter with 3 USB Charging Ports (1 USB-C, 2 USB A), Multi Plug Outlets Wall Mount with Top Phone Holder for Home, Dorm Essentail, 490 Joules

ECOSUSI Women's Briefcase Vegan Leather Laptop Bag for Work Shoulder Computer Satchel Bag with Detachable Bow [[VIDEOID:307ef2b77a12b4ad7a2e151ce52ffd72]]This is an elegant ladies laptop messenger bag/briefcase made of attractive PU leather with delicate cutout design work across the front and a bow that adds a nice feminine touch to a professional looking bag. I ordered the blue color which has a rich consistent tone that's true to the product picture on this page. I think it looks even more attractive in hand than in the product photos and I think the antique brass hardware compliments it very nicely as well.

The bag offers three carry options: handbag, shoulder bag, or cross body, and measures approximately 14.2 x 10.2 x 3.9 inches. It's a fairly simple design with all of the storage inside the main compartment and no storage on the outside of the bag. The bag has a large fold over flap with two magnetic snaps that latch it closed. I found that I had to move the flap around some to position it so that the magnets closed together, and it took more effort when the bag was loaded with gear so that's a slight inconvenience at times.

The flap also extends down nearly to the bottom of the bag which makes it awkward to access the main compartment easily when carrying the bag. Although the flap looks attractive, I would prefer that it was only half as long in order to offer more convenient access to the main compartment.

The main compartment has a zippered close top that glides open and closed easily, and the entire interior is lined in a rich brown colored cotton material. I like that because the dark color won't show ink stains or dirt so it will continue to look nice much longer than a lighter fabric would. The front wall of the main compartment has two cell phone or other small device pockets, and the back wall has a padded compartment for a small laptop or tablet that's 12" across followed by a 7" x 5" zippered compartment immediately behind that.

Besides holding a small laptop or tablet in the padded compartment, the interior of the bag is spacious enough to easily hold project folders, presentation materials, books, another tablet, power cords, adapters and other gear. You can carry this bag by the sturdy handle, or attach the adjustable shoulder straps so you can carry it as a shoulder bag, or increase the strap length to carry it cross body.

All stitching appears to be very well done with reinforcement at all attachment and stress points, and the lobster claw strap hardware is very secure once attached. Zippers open and close smoothly and are well attached. The only downsides about this bag in my opinion are the large awkward front flap and the somewhat weak magnetic snaps. Otherwise, the bag looks feminine without looking too girly, although I'm undecided about that bow. It definitely looks professional enough to carry on campus or into business meetings, and certainly seems well made. Enjoy!

This ladies briefcase/ laptop messenger bag was provided by Ecosusi for evaluation and review. I hope that my inspection and observations about it prove helpful with your decision making.
text_fidelity_b: ECOSUSI Women's Briefcase Vegan Leather Laptop Bag for Work Shoulder Computer Satchel Bag with Detachable Bow

Monoprice VGA to RCA Adapter PC to TV Video Converter- Blue I realize this was a cheap item, manufactured over seas, but after reading many of the reviews, I took a chance anyway. First issue was, like many other reviewers, it was shipped without the USB power cord. I emailed the seller to inform them but as an IT guy, i have tons of these around the house so it wasn't too big of a deal. After getting it all hooked up to an old fashion tube tv, like many others, the screen was black and white, flickering and illegible. i hooked it to a flat screen tv, changed it to NTSC, and was able to see the on screen menu but no picture, only gray bars. I tweaked all the menu options but was never able to see a picture. I made note of the options and reconnected it to my tube TV but after more than 45 minutes trying every combination of options i could, i was never able to get a picture. i've already printed a return label and will send it back tomorrow.

Update: after requesting a return from Amazon and shipping the unit back, I received a response from the seller (keep in mind he did not know that the unit didn't work, only that it did not come with a power cord) His suggestion was to ask Amazon for a refund and order another unit. So let us assume the unit actually did work, He would have wanted me to initiate a return with amazon, print out a label, drop the item off at UPS, spend more money (until i get my refund) to order another unit and cross my fingers that the new one comes with all the pieces. Why not do what any respectable business would do and just send me a power cord?
text_fidelity_b: Monoprice VGA to RCA Adapter PC to TV Video Converter- Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Acer C720 Chromebook (11.6-Inch, 2GB) **Discontinued by Manufacturer** These are pretty much the perfect laptop for kids (and adults too if they don't want to download or install any personal programs). The Google App store has just about every type of app/program you could want. These don't have a DVD drive and you can't download programs unless they are from the App store. It's a good way of keeping your machine safe from malware attacks. No need to purchase and renew antiviral software. The screen is clear and bright, and the keyboard works really nicely. The sound from these is much better than the sound on my much more expensive laptop. Overall, the size and functionality of the Chromebook is much better than my new Windows 8.1 laptop.

My kids were able to get started immediately with minimal help from me to download some apps they like, get their e-mails set up and started using these Chromebooks immediately. I personally am not nuts about having only Google Chrome as my internet browser, thus I don't own my own Chromebook, but for my kids purposes (mainly games and schoolwork) the Chromebooks work out great. I really like how easy and smoothly they work. They are faster than my laptop and I do find that appealing, but I like being able to use a DVD drive and to be able to download what software I might want from the internet.

Printing is possible from the cloud and set up to do that is not difficult. Everything is easy........almost too easy. You can't store any data on the computer itself, only in the cloud. But, I'm not worried about any personal information being accessed by nefarious types because there's really nothing to access.

We've had these Chromebooks since Christmas and they are still working fine with no problems whatsoever.

UPDATE: 2.28.15 - My daughter brought it to my attention that these chromebooks do not have a "delete" key. Interesting.
text_fidelity_b: Acer C720 Chromebook (11.6-Inch, 2GB) **Discontinued by Manufacturer**

text_fidelity_a:
Blink Indoor Home Security Camera System with Motion Detection, HD Video, 2-Year Battery Life and Cloud Storage Included - 3 Camera Kit In terms of installation, it really doesn't get any easier: basically just plug in the control module and tap a couple buttons to register each camera and you're in business. Took me all of 5 minutes.

The cameras themselves aren't feature rich - you're not going to find tilt/swivel/zoom or even night vision. But you can't expect it from cameras that operate in 2 AA for up to 2 years! They do what they're designed to do: basic monitoring with motion detection in a completely wireless setup (you can literally place the cameras anywhere!). An LED light can illuminate any recording in darkness.

There's no monthly service fee either - but the recordings you can take are only up to a minute long and there's a limit on how many.

I love these cameras for their ease of setup and complete mobility. The only reason I'm not giving them 5 stars is the lack of an outdoor camera option and a little bit buggy iOS app.

Update (11/27/2017): a couple negatives to the cameras:
(1) while each camera comes with a wall mount, orienting it just right (in my case on a front porch so I could see who's at the door) isn't all that easy (just because the camera doesn't have an area in its view doesn't mean it won't detect motion slightly outside it!)
(2) the cameras have no speakers. I knew this when buying, of course, but competing cameras in same price range do.
(3) I just asked Blink whether there are any plans for Apple HomeKIt support - and there aren't :-( This is a big negative for me because I'm starting to do some home automation and since we're an Apple household, I want HomeKit. So I'm going to be looking for another set of cameras instead of expanding my Blink set :-(
text_fidelity_b: Blink Indoor Home Security Camera System with Motion Detection, HD Video, 2-Year Battery Life and Cloud Storage Included - 3 Camera Kit

text_fidelity_a:
THINKWARE TW-X350 Dash Cam with 1080P Sony Exmor Sensor, Wi-Fi, & 2.7" LCD Screen Frustrating. Could not get the iPhone app to work at all, I'd slide the WiFi button to be informed that the WiFi was not functioning. Do I need to set up a local hotspot to use the WiFi feature to download the videos? Which appears to be about the only distinguishing feature of this dashcam. This is NOT a Sony product, apparently it uses licensed Sony technology. The dashcam itself is reasonably well designed. There's a horrid mechanical-female voice which I don't see how to disable. The user experience overall is poor. The manual is not bad as far as legibility, but the content is minimum. Minimal content in four or five languages.

The mounting scheme is atrocious, a joke. I'm not going to put self-adhesive cable anchors anywhere in my car, period. It's just plain dumb. I'm tempted to use a suction cup mount from another dashcam. Or cable ties on my rear-view mirror. But if you're homebrewing a solution right out of the box, maybe you're better off with another product altogether. The mounting suggestion is just a show-stopper. Not a good thing.

The video itself seems good, I mean, dashcams in general are fascinating and useful. But if you're expecting to have consumers put something in their car, it had been not involve defacing any part of the car or reducing its value. Leftover adhesive footprints would be an obvious problem.

I'm uploading a photo of the box. Green type on a black background. Not really a great design. Generally type and packaging tells you more about a product than the manufacturer might have intended. Just not that sophisticated.

Overall there are better dashcams out there. The ability to use WiFi to download video from the camera seemed promising, but I couldn't get it to work at all. The audio feedback from the device was far too loud and I couldn't turn it off. The mounting idea was dead on arrival, not happening.

Disappointing. Cannot recommend this product. A swing and a miss, as they say in baseball.
text_fidelity_b: THINKWARE TW-X350 Dash Cam with 1080P Sony Exmor Sensor, Wi-Fi, & 2.7" LCD Screen

Loved this cooling pad -- I used it under my gaming laptop on which I gamed and did data analysis/coding, and it kept my computer cool. Without it, my laptop would quickly reach over 82 C, with the cooling pad it was kept right around 70 C.
I bought it in January of 2021 and it lasted until December 2021, almost a year. I loved it so much I'm considering rebuying it, but I wish I knew why it crapped out on me. It's not expensive or anything, and I did use it for 8-10 hours a day (and a couple times I forgot to turn it off so it was on all night), but still... I wish it had lasted longer. I never used anything less than full-fan, and kept it tilted for air flow. There is a little bumper you can flip up to hold your laptop in place, but I found my laptop needed to be a bit more forward than the bumper allowed (to get the best air flow into the system) so I always kept it down and my laptop scooted forward -- still never slid off. One day I turn it on it the screen goes blue but the fans don't come on, no text is on the screen, and I can't get the lights to turn off unless it's unplugged. Not sure what happened, but there wasn't a power surge or anything.
Overall, I'd give it 5 stars if it just lasted a LEAST a year or so... But the thought of having to repurchase this yearly annoys me so it gets 3 stars.

text_fidelity_a:
WixGear Sport Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.0 Wireless Over Ear Sport Headphones with Touch Control, and Charging Case Stereo Deep Bass Sound,30H Playtime Sweat-Proof Bluetooth Earphones with Mic For my uses, these are great. They were very well packaged and secure for shipping. The box is very nice and sturdy, lined with foam. I need to hear the environment around me. This has been an issue with previous earbuds. Commercials between videos or songs can get so loud! That is the deal-breaker for me, as it's a safety issue. These do not get too loud, even on the loudest setting, so I am able to remain safe. I don't have an issue hearing the sounds coming from the buds, but I'm not in high-traffic outdoor areas regularly either. My ear canals are unusually small for an adult. I was afraid these may be too-big, but they are snug. Any bigger and it may have been an issue. I used the smaller of the plastic tips. Over the ear designs are the only ones that have ever worked for me. I did look at some other models in the past, but I found them a bit more expensive than I felt justified to spend unknowing how well they may work for me. However, knowing how well these work, I find them to be a really great value and would have purchased them before if I had known how well they worked. It was only by chance they were up for review and I had been seeking a replacement on my old pair that I've been using for the past few years.

The Bluetooth is nice. I have a simple cell phone. It only took asking my phone to connect to work. It was the easiest that I have ever had with connecting anything Bluetooth to my phone. I liked this as I'm not the most savvy at using Bluetooth electronics. If I can do it, anyone can.

I'm not great at using the buttons as they are really sensors on the flat-side of the body on the earbuds. I'm getting used to it but they are touch sensitive and there is a correct spot and amount of pressure that works best. I'm still getting a feel for it and there is a slight delay, so it's very easy to double-tap. The included booklet has been helpful to learn to use these straight out of the package.

Sometimes I get down on the floor at the gym to use the foam rollers and stretches, other times I'm using them in the car to take calls. I've tried them at work as well. Every scenario has worked well for me. I really do wish I've had these before. Sometimes while getting my breaks at work, I would want to listen to things from my phone, but didn't want to risk disturbing my co-workers with some of the news and hobby related videos I enjoy. I asked a few co-workers if they could hear my earbud noise, they could not.

The case is very easy to use as well and fits easily into my pockets. I'm a lady, so my pockets are not always very generously sized. It charges very quickly, and I've not found myself running out of charge. I cannot speak on the long-term durability for this as they are new. If/when I experience any issues with the charge, I will be sure to post an update.

In summary, these would be better for users that need to hear their surroundings for safety. For those that want extreme high volume, they may not be as happy. They stay on my ears securely and the case works very well. I'm pleasantly surprised how well I like these and hope that they are durable since they are working so well for me.

Thanks for reading my review. I hope you found it helpful.
text_fidelity_b: WixGear Sport Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.0 Wireless Over Ear Sport Headphones with Touch Control, and Charging Case Stereo Deep Bass Sound,30H Playtime Sweat-Proof Bluetooth Earphones with Mic

Aurum Cables Pack of 2 AUX 3.5mm Male to 3.5mm Male Stereo Audio Cable - for iPhone, iPad or Smartphones - 12 Feet I received this pack as a review sample and quickly came to the conclusion that these are excellent for noise-free applications. The most critical test was when I used this cable to connect a pair of [[ASIN:B006MA9XXM Brainwavz HM5 Studio Monitor Headphones]] to my stereo. The sound was as neutral and noise free as when I used the high grade cable that came with the phones, so the claim of double shielding hold weight. I would not hesitate to recommend these to audiophiles or sound engineers.

In addition to the listening test I thoroughly inspected the physical characteristics. That revealed attention to detail like what appears to be copper cladding or gold plating on the tip, ring and sleeve portions of the connector. The barrel housing is also well constructed and is probably stainless steel. The strain reliefs on the ends are also well done and should protect the ends from internal breakdown even if you frequently handle the cable. The cable itself will stretch to a full twelve feet, but at rest is a little over a foot and a half.

What I did not test is the claim that this will fit most phones through their case. That's because the cases that I have on hand will accommodate regular cables. There is a chamfer on the barrel that houses the connector and it looks as though it will fit some of the more finicky iPhone 5 cases, but I cannot guarantee that it will for all cases.

These are top quality cables that should last a long time if properly handled and stored. If I do experience a premature failure I'll update this review to reflect that.
text_fidelity_b: Aurum Cables Pack of 2 AUX 3.5mm Male to 3.5mm Male Stereo Audio Cable - for iPhone, iPad or Smartphones - 12 Feet

I've purchased a few of these. One did fail after a few years of intense use (I play Diablo 3 and a few MMOs, along with regular productivity/internet surfing.) Considering the price, and the amount of use these get, I have nothing but praise for these devices.

I will be honest: I reluctantly purchased this device. I've been using trackballs since around 1997 because my original computer space didn't really accommodate a standard mouse, and I really haven't gone back to mice. The corded Logitech Trackman has been my favored trackball for years. My cat chewed through the cord, and it eventually stopped working right, so I had to upgrade. Having a wireless trackball has always seemed rather redundant to me; why would you need cordless when you never move it? Well, it's actually quite nice to not fiddle with the cord! I didn't realize how annoying having a tether is until you no longer have it...

At any rate, this trackball is remarkably accurate (I play several games and work with large spread sheets,) and a snap to install. In short, a reluctant customer is very satisfied!

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Surface Book 13.5" (Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM, 256 GB) We have a number of surface tablets in our house, and this was my first surface book. I got it hoping for some increased performance for using with my landscape CAD program, and I did notice a difference in the smoothness when working with CAD on this device as opposed to my other comparable surface tablets. The better performance only works when it is hooked up to the keyboard, which is fine for CAD work.

I also like to use this as a tablet for photo editing work related to my business, and here I noticed my number one complaint about this device, which is that the tablet part itself does not have the little foldout stand that all of the other surface tablets have. I guess they think that you will just connect it to the keyboard, but sometimes I want it to be as flexible and lightweight as a regular surface Pro tablet, and while you can unhook it from the keyboard and use it as a tablet, it feels more bulky and the lack of stand makes it less flexible in its use than the surface Pro tablets.

One thing I did notice is that you can connect it to the keyboard backwards and use the keyboard as a stand that way, however that does not bend to the same angle as the tablet stands do on a regular surface Pro.

I also think that the battery life is a lot less on this one than on the surface Pro tablets. Even when not connected to the keyboard and the increased computing performance that you get from that, it seems to wear down its batteries on tablet mode in about 30 to 45 minutes of photo editing. When I worked on my surface tablet in this fashion, I feel like I got a little less than two hours before having to recharge.

Overall, if you plan to use this primarily plugged in as a laptop and only occasionally as a tablet, the increased performance from the attached keyboard make this a worthwhile choice if you do gaming or more high-powered computing. However, if you are primarily using it as a tablet or in places where battery life is a critical consideration, I would suggest the regular surface Pro tablet instead.

In terms of accessories, I use the surface pen constantly, but haven't reached for the other accessories much at all. The surface pen makes it so smooth to make notes on photographs to convey ideas to people, and is great for photo editing.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Surface Book 13.5" (Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM, 256 GB)

text_fidelity_a:
Moshi iVisor XT (HD clear) No-Bubble Screen Protector for the Fire HDX 8.9" I purchased this protector due to the overwhelming positive reports from other verified buyers. I do not like my cell phone's screen being unprotected and now with my first Kindle I feel the same way. The HDX screen is gorgeous and I want a way to keep it as such. This screen protector seemed the answer to my predicament.

This protector is, indeed, extremely simple to 'install'. It takes more time to remove it from its packaging and throw the trash away afterwards than it does to apply the protector itself. Simply line up the cutouts on the protector film with the camera and flash at the top and center of your Kindle and you are done. I found it helpful to guide the film into place by kind of rolling the sides down, guiding them to ensure proper placement. Then just apply a little pressure (basically, run your hand around the edges) to activate the adhesive.

Only the outer black margin of the protector has adhesive to stick it to the border and outer edges of your Kindle, thus leaving the clear center which covers your Kindle's screen loose, or non-sticky. This manufacturing and design approach has both pros and one con I have noticed so far.

Pros:

It allows for lightning fast and super easy installation.

Because of the solid black border, you can accidentally touch the sticky side while installing and lining it up without any fingerprints showing through as with a normal screen protector. This was a bonus to me as these things are always so difficult to install without this happening.

The clear center portion that covers the screen is completely 100% bubble free.

Due to some micro hairs/fibers being on the screen despite having wiped it down prior to installing the protector, I learned that I could remove the protector (lifted up one corner and peeled it halfway back to do a quick swipe with the MF cloth again) and it would re-adhere to the Kindle's surface just as well as it did the first time.

The company claims that, if it should lose its stickiness, the protector can be rinsed/washed and used again. I have yet to need to go this far so I cannot comment on the credit-worthiness of this claim, however from my experiences so far, I can see the possibility of this claim holding up.

I have not noticed any blurring or the rainbow affect the company mentions on its packaging. The screen is crystal clear and appears to not even have a screen protector on it.

Con:

Since the clear center portion does not adhere to the screen, it is allowed to float just above the screen thus reducing the screen sensitivity and requiring more force from either your fingertip or your stylus.

After using my Kindle for a few hours after installation of this screen protector, I have come to the above conclusions. As bad as the con is for me and my preferences, I will leave it on for a few days to give myself a little more time and to see if anything changes. This screen protector ranks very high on my list of desirable protectors (I even searched to see if they make a version for my Droid cell phone) so I am really hoping that the sensitivity issue works itself out soon.
text_fidelity_b: Moshi iVisor XT (HD clear) No-Bubble Screen Protector for the Fire HDX 8.9"

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon AF-S DX NIKKOR 55-300mm f/4.5-5.6G ED Vibration Reduction Zoom Lens with Auto Focus for Nikon DSLR Cameras This is my current go-to lens. I wish I could afford one of the more fancy-schmancy professional telephotos, but until then, this one is the one parked on my Nikon D7000.

Uses:

1. Birds, bugs and other critters from a safe distance or on the fly/run
2. Portraits of one or two people (gives excellent bokeh)
3. Landscapes and seascapes, especially in vertical/portrait mode.

Limitations:

1. Buildings from across-the-street distance
2. Large groups of people
3. Macro shots from thisclose

Depending on the type of photography you enjoy, this may or may not be the lens for you. It works fine for me for the uses above, especially when the subjects are a respectable distance away, but it doesn't have a wide enough angle for limitations 1 and 2, and if you're closer than a couple of feet it won't focus properly.

It's also pretty heavy, but makes up for this by making you look like a pro who knows what they're about, especially when you use the lens hood (included and highly recommended for use)

The auto-focus is not as smooth as it should be, and you can sometimes hear the mechanism moving around trying to do its job, but image stabilization and the tripod detection mode are huge pluses. (It also attaches/detaches from the camera in the opposite direction to my other (Sigma) lens)

For the type of photography I'm doing at the moment. even if it's not on the camera, this lens goes with me wherever I roam.

Amanda Richards, March 30, 2012
text_fidelity_b: Nikon AF-S DX NIKKOR 55-300mm f/4.5-5.6G ED Vibration Reduction Zoom Lens with Auto Focus for Nikon DSLR Cameras

Lexar NM600 M.2 2280 NVMe 480GB Solid-State Drive (LNM600-480RBNA) Modern computers are a lot more reliable than computers from 10 or 20 years ago. Computers are not getting a lot faster every year like they used to. I no longer replace my computer every couple of years. If your computer is getting a little sluggish, instead of replacing the whole thing, you can usually give it a huge performance boost by upgrading just key components. In particular, upgrade your memory and upgrade your hard drive. This SSD does not add a lot of capacity, but it gives you a lot of speed so that programs or databases that you use a lot will load much more quickly.

This drive installed and formatted easily on my Windows 10 desktop computer. It's been running flawlessly since then and the performance is great for me. Performance is great for general-purpose home or business use.

There are a lot of different SSDs on the market these days. Check your computer manufacturer's website to see what is compatible with your motherboard. This SSD has an entry-level design and a budget price to match. High-performance SSDs designed for hard-core gaming or video editing can be twice as fast but also cost twice as much or more for the same capacity.

The E4200 does a much better job, actually the RT-N56U fails miserably when trying to backup using Windows backup to a USB drive (NTFS or FAT32). It seems they do not have plans to make this work in the future.

Unfortunately their customer service do not offer too much help.

Following you will find how they answered a question I submitted regarding the USB attached drives issue:

My question:
I have been trying to use Windows Backup with a drive attached via USB to this unit. I
have tried different hard drives formatted both as FAT32 and NTFS. Backups always
fail. Mostly with Error code: 0x80070008. Is there a compatibility issue between this
router and Windows Backup? I still have two weeks to return this router if I cannot
make it work.

Their response:
The router has its own settings that will operate reguardless if the computer works or not. The computer has nothing to do with the router software one way or the other. If you need to back up the router setting then I suggest you take screen shots of the router to verify that you can save the settings from there.
Thanks Aaron Asus Support Team

Well, I am still trying to figure out what their response means...

Do not get this router if you need USB features. They do not work.

text_fidelity_a:
Upgrade/RGB Video Light, 360 ° Full Color LED Camera Light, Dimmable 2500K-8500K Portable Pocket Size Camera Lighting, 12 Lighting Effect Mode, Built-in 3200mAh Rechargeable Battery We do jewelry photos which are very difficult to shoot, especially when iridescence is involved. We have big lights to set up and get good shots, but then we have been having issues with some of the light leaving things looking a bit dead. Enter this light. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This a light that is about the size of a smart phone- well the slightly larger ones. It comes with a case that has an elastic band on one side and a net bag with elastic top on the opposite side. The kit comes with a square slide to put on the camera along with screws to hold the discs in place to stop wobble. There is a charge outlet,, a charge cord (USB on the other end) and an output cord which goes from C to USB.

HOW DOES THIS WORK?
When you turn this on, you press the power button and hold it down. The light goes on. There is a little window with the information in it.

TIME LEFT FOR USE
This tells you how many hours are left before you need to recharge so you can plan your sessions.

BATTERY
There is a battery indicator

BRIGHTNESS
From 5% to 100%

TEMPERATURE
Coolest temp being 5600K down to 3200K which is like candlelight.

DIAL
The dial on the side allows you to go up or down

POWER BUTTON DUAL MENU BUTTON
You use the power button to turn on the light, but once it is on, then if you touch it once quickly, it changes from brightness to temperature so you can set what you like. An arrow is very obvious so you know where it is set.

HOW TO ATTACH TO CAMERA
I have a Canon Poweshot G12 and this attaches up where a flash usually goes. You can screw this into the lamp either horizontally or vertically. You slide in the metal plate with the screw on it, then you screw the light onto that and use the discs to tighten up the light so it does not move.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
I have to say, this little thing is amazing. It has fantastic light, works very well and even though you can use it by itself for video or interviews, etc, for jewelry photos, we need to have additional light to use with this to avoid shadows.

I have gotten some excellent photos which are really nice and with a little adjustments in photo editing turn out to be great in capturing texture, color, and iridescence.

CHARGING
I found that a few hours of charging gave me a complete charge. After using this for about three hours (I turned it off in between set ups) I still have four out of five bars on the battery indicator and about 4 hours left of predicted use time.

WILL I NEED ANOTHER LIGHT?
If you are doing product photos like we are of jewelry or something that is detailed and needs to have very good lighting, then you will probably need another light. I would say a second one of these would be perfect- set it up on a little tripod and it will be great. If you are just doing portraits, or interviews, you might be able to get away with just this light. Shadows at that point don't matter as much- unless they are severe, of course.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is one of the best things I have ever gotten for taking photos. It has really helped me take photos beautifully an I am thrilled with it. The temperature control is beautiful and the brightness controls are also excellent in increments.

MY RATING
FIVE VERY ENTHUSIASTIC STARS. This is a great portable light that goes with you anywhere. The case is great, and the light is the perfect size to toss into my camera bag when traveling.

PHOTOS
When I get some photos that I am not using on my site, I will try to post some for you. It is worth seeing.
text_fidelity_b: Upgrade/RGB Video Light, 360 ° Full Color LED Camera Light, Dimmable 2500K-8500K Portable Pocket Size Camera Lighting, 12 Lighting Effect Mode, Built-in 3200mAh Rechargeable Battery

Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) Let's begin with the cons:
This is NOT an Android tablet, even tho it looks like it. You CAN NOT download apps from the Google Play Store (at least, not without jumping through some hoops), the apps available on the Amazon Apps are sorely lacking in some areas (many of the apps I use and really like on Google Play are not available), the OS is slow and clumsy, the home screen is not particularly user friendly and the HOME button is only accessed through a screen, not a dedicated button, which makes it a pain in the butt (sometimes, not always.)
Now, for the pros:
Good size for a personal tablet, very durable screen and housing, and the biggest pro is the price! I got mine on sale for $39.99, and for that price, I honestly wasn't expecting a whole lot. I'm disappointed with the OS, but as a starter-level tablet, if you want to read books, surf the internet, check your email and engage in social networking, it's fine. I RECOMMEND it, even at the full price of $49.99, because for that price, you are NOT going to find any kind of name-brand table (BEWARE OF THE WEIRD, OFF-BRAND TABLETS! I'VE BOUGHT 3 FOR GRANDDAUGHTER'S USE WHEN THEY COME TO VISIT, AND NOT A SINGLE ONE LASTED MORE THAN A FEW MONTHS) for even a third of the price. Just don't expect the same experience you may be used to on your Android smartphone or tablets that you now have.

text_fidelity_a:
Monocular High Power Spotting Scope - Baronage 12X42 High Definition Telescope with Smartphone Tripod and Phone Mount Adapter for Adults Bird Watching Camping Travelling. This BARONAGE MONOCULAR TELESCOPE (12X42 High Power BAK4 Prism, with Tripod and Phone Mount Adapter) delivers a lot of bang for the bucks (it costs about $30 on Amazon). It’s pocket-sized (about 6” long, 4” wide), provides good magnification, and comes with both a mini-tripod and a smartphone mount.

The magnification is quite good. The little telescope is great for hand-held viewing of nearby objects of interest. The focus wheel works smoothly, and it is positioned to be very easy to use.

You’ll probably want to use a tripod for taking smartphone photos (though I took some decent photos without one). The photos are pretty good, even if all you do is point, focus (looking at the smartphone display), and shoot. (You won’t be taking prize-winning nature photos with this monocular telescope, but the photos are fine for documenting a trip or other interesting sightings.)

In the attached photos, the tree closeup shows the tree seen in the top center of the second photo (which was taken from the same spot with the smartphone camera alone). The tree closeup appears more sharply focused in my camera gallery than it does here on Amazon; some of the detail was dropped during Amazon's processing.

MOUNTING NOTES: The telescope doesn’t come with instructions for assembling the smartphone mount, or for attaching the telescope to the tripod (see the product page for these). Note that the little projection on the telescope (actually a loop for attaching a lanyard) can be unscrewed to reveal a threaded hole for attaching the tripod.

Also, note that the smartphone mount uses a threaded piece (a round cap with a threaded hole) that screws onto the flat positioning bar that allows you to adjust the position of your smartphone and its camera lens. It’s easy to overlook the cap’s fine threads. The round cap piece fits over the viewer end of the telescope to hold the smartphone clamped in the mount’s pull-out jaws. The mount worked fine with my Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge, and I didn’t even have to take the phone out of its Otterbox Symmetry case.
text_fidelity_b: Monocular High Power Spotting Scope - Baronage 12X42 High Definition Telescope with Smartphone Tripod and Phone Mount Adapter for Adults Bird Watching Camping Travelling.

SAMSUNG Galaxy Buds Live True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds w/ Active Noise Cancelling, Charging Case, AKG Tuned 12mm Speaker, Long Battery Life, US Version, Mystic Red I bought mine direct from Samsung and ultimately returned them. I found that I had to fiddle with them constantly to hit the sweet spot for the music to sound like it should instead of like I was listening through a tin can, and while fiddling with them the touch controls become an annoying hassle because you are trying to get the fit right and the music is turning on and off and pausing and skipping, etc, because you are touching them. The buds can't seem to differentiate at all between an actual hold/grip to manipulate them in your ears, and a tap as you would do to actually use a touch control feature.

Don't quote me on this because it's not like I counted every review that appeared male vs female, but I found that they hurt and I think it might be because they were designed by somewhat larger-eared males. I originally assumed the hurty issue was likely because they were designed by some 60 year old man engineer with huge ears (because ears grow our whole lives) and so they were only made to fit kind of older larger ears. I even wrote on my Samsung review that they should have made the fit for the age group of their customer. But now, reading these Amazon reviews, I am noticing that the people saying they fit great seem to mostly be male names and those saying they hurt seem to mostly be female-normative names, so I still think they were designed for larger ears, but maybe for males they will fit better - I truly don't know how different in size male vs female ears are though; it's just a random observation of these reviews of hurt vs feel great.

Bottom line, they hurt my ears and were too picky about being perfectly aligned in my ear. On the rare occasion I hit that sweet spot they sounded great and never felt like they were going to fall out. Too bad it took so much effort to find that spot.
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG Galaxy Buds Live True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds w/ Active Noise Cancelling, Charging Case, AKG Tuned 12mm Speaker, Long Battery Life, US Version, Mystic Red

text_fidelity_a:
Certified Refurbished Kindle Paperwhite E-reader - White, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 7th) I stopped reading as much when my eyes got old and tired. I finally broke down and bought a Kindle, and it's been a game-changer. I'm blowing through books again! Overall, it's been very helpful.

Pros and cons are:

Pros:
- can enlarge fonts as needed so it's easier on my eyes
- Paperwhite backlighting is also really easy on the eyes; I don't get fatigued and can read anywhere, night or day
- can download a crap ton of books and only carry the one small device
- great battery life

Cons:
- miss the tactile aspect of turning pages, skipping back and forth, feeling in your hands how much book you have left
- can't remember as well where a passage is in the book because I don't have mental image of where it was on the page, and about how many pages in it was
- touchscreen is kind of spazzy and sometimes will change font size on me or if I accidentally brush against the screen while reading -- this has been the most annoying bit
- touchscreen is also kind of slow: I touch something, it takes a moment to react; by this time I think it hasn't registered so I touch it again, only to have it do something twice and take me somewhere else, and I end up lost

Generally speaking though, the pros outweigh the cons, so I will keep loading books on this little guy!
text_fidelity_b: Certified Refurbished Kindle Paperwhite E-reader - White, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 7th)

text_fidelity_a:
iHome iAVS16 Bedside Speaker with Alexa Built In, Bluetooth, and USB Charging, Now Supports Spotify by Voice This is a pretty mixed review of an interesting concept that is pretty good right now, but has the potential to be great in the near future. At the current price of about $150, this is ok+ based on the following criteria:

Sound Quality: 2.5-3 stars
For the size, it's ok
When reviewing for sound quality, I compare speakers (and headphones) to comparably sized items, based on speakers I currently or previously have owned. I take price range *somewhat* into account (I don't expect $15 headphones to sound like $500 ones), but for anything over $100, I use the full range from the cheapest stuff I have, to my favorite brand, Bose.
So with that in mind, I have a portable wireless Bose speaker that is smaller and acts as the "5" on the scale.
The sound on this can get loud enough to not distort and still fill a smallish room or normal bedroom fine. The treble and bass are ok, though the higher ranges are tinny and the bass lacks depth. Overall sound from high to low and throughout the mid range lack definition. It's good enough for very casual background listening and for podcasts.

Alexa Feature: 4 stars
I have an iPhone and think Alexa has quite a bit more understanding and skill than Siri. When asked questions, from simple stuff like "what's the weather" to more complicated stuff like "I'm hungry. What can I make in half an hour?", the answers and follow-up questions are highly intuitive and thorough. Does she get everything all the time? No. But she does a much better job than Siri.

User-Friendliness: 2.5 stars
I didn't like the process of figuring out how this works, particularly the part of pairing with more than one device and also Having to use an app to make most of it work. It was a clunky, irritating process that more or less stayed that way every time I wanted to use this thing, especially for listening to music. It should be able to just play from your iTunes through the iTunes app and bluetooth, and instead, I was only able to make it play iTunes though Their App, which sucks when it comes to my music. And that brings us to the App..

App: 2 stars
No. Just no. Bluetooth exists for a reason, and if a speaker has bluetooth, you should be able to just pair and play. I had to use the app to play from my iTunes, and because I have a very specific way of organizing things, I was incredibly annoyed that something didn't translate, and my music was disorganized and basically impossible to search for with this app. Instead of being able to play what I want from one of my playlist subfolders, it disregarded my way of organizing things, and I ended up giving up. If I can't listen to my stuff easily with this, then like 75% of the reason to use this disappears, leaving me with an expensive alarm clock with weather report, recipe ideas, and some cool internet stuff. That's cool, but it's quite incomplete for what I need, and what I suspect many people want.

tl;dr version: sound is mediocre but doable, app is bad, Alexa is super clever and smart, and the experience has a lot of frustrating aspects.
text_fidelity_b: iHome iAVS16 Bedside Speaker with Alexa Built In, Bluetooth, and USB Charging, Now Supports Spotify by Voice

text_fidelity_a:
D-Link Wi-Fi Camera with Remote Viewing (DCS-930L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) Compared to a similar camera made by Belkin, setting up the D-Link was kind of a pain. Not as much of a pain as setting up a Foscam F18918W - where you get directed to a third party domain name provider and get to learn the joys of port forwarding - but a relative hassle.

For the Belkin, I opened the box, plugged into my router, ran a set up program that took less than five minutes, downloaded an app, and I was up and running. While this is a very similar product in both look and function, it took over an hour - and two ethernet cables - to set it up. There is no Mac software on the installation cd. The box states that a Windows pc is required, but the website has a Mac download available. You have to scroll through the product photos, which aren't in alphanumeric order. Just keep looking until you find the DCS-930L - AFTER the 931L and the 932L and the 934L. Have faith. Keep going. It's there.

Once you get the program installed, it takes very little time to *find* the camera and teach it to log into your wireless network. And then you are back to the website to set up your account and view your camera. Except you are on a Mac, and the viewer requires you to install the Java Runtime Environment. JRE is a big old security vulnerability on Macs. So much so that Apple advises against using it. Mavericks lets you turn it on case by case - and, by default, it will ask you every time before running it. If you are on an OS below Mavericks, check the googles for setting your preferences so that you're not running JRE all the time.

Okay, so now you've got JRE going, and the first thing the program tells you is that you have to update your firmware AND you need to have the camera AND your computer ethernet-jacked right into your router. LOLWUT? I'm lucky. I am on a laptop, and I have an extra ethernet cable and an empty port. So, I did that, and there I was, up and running, about an hour, hour and a half, thereabouts, after I started.

Image quality is pretty good - not great. Audio is okay. The settings are very customizable. But the wifi receiver is very weak, and that limits the usefulness of this product.
text_fidelity_b: D-Link Wi-Fi Camera with Remote Viewing (DCS-930L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

1MORE Quad Driver in-Ear Earphones Hi-Res High Fidelity Headphones Warm Bass, Spacious Reproduction, High Resolution, Mic in-Line Remote Smartphones/PC/Tablet - Silver/Gray I am not an audiophile by any means. I have Rockbox installed on my iPod video classic with a FiiO amp attached, all loaded with FLAC tunes. I listen to Spotify at work. That's the extent of my musical needs.
I have Audio-Technica headphones, and dream of some day owning custom Kaisers. That's my background.

I was pretty excited to get these. Right after ordering, I watched a few YouTube videos on them, and read up on Head-Fi. For the price, 1More seems to deliver outstanding products. Needless to say, I was pretty excited.

The box finally came and I was found to be very impressed with the presentation. You get a nice, magnetic box housing the IEMs, a leather(ette?) pouch, and multiple choices of ear piece tips. For starters, I found that the ear piece tips pre-attached to the IEMs were the most fitted for me, but I still do not find them perfect. They slide down a bit when in my ear, so there is some loss of sound. I will have to buy some aftermarket ones.

The microphone is also sub-par. This is the first time I've used a mic with headphones, and most of my calls could not catch my voice properly. I would get complaints that I sounded muffled or far away, and so I've resorted to using the phone mic most of the time. The mic buttons work flawlessly for playback features, however.

As for the sound, it's fantastic. With four drivers, I can hear so much more--and so many more flaws! I usually transfer music files into FLAC, and so I have pretty good sources for music. I've been using both my Samsung Galaxy S5 and Rockboxed iPod Video (equipped with a Fiio E11), and the sounds are great, but I'm noticing some files that weren't transferred correctly. I cannot connect to my computer speakers at work as the speakers do not have enough power to juice up the Quads, so be sure you have a more recent device or one with enough power to drive these IEMs.

Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones - Ivory I'm normally an ear bud user since I've never been able to find an over the ear headset that was comfortable to wear for more than 10 minutes or so at a time. Well, I found one - these are undoubtable the most comfortable headphones I've ever used. Just a dream to wear even for extended periods of time. Light, cushy, just right. And they look so elegant - a nice change from the sparse industrial look that electronics often have.

Construction quality seems very good, especially the cord (a common point of failure for me with any type of earphones). It comes with the regular and mini size plugs.

The sound quality is absolutly top-notch. I'm not an audiophile, so I can't throw out the phrases and jargon I typically read in audio discussion boards and magazines (well, I can throw them out, but not with any semblance of knowing what I'm taking about). So suffice it to say that I can't imagine anyone not being very pleased with the quality of sound using these and a MP3 player or an iPad (the two devices I've used with them so far). I've been absolutely amazed at how great these sound.

My only complaint is the lack of sound isolation. Outside sounds can easily be heard. Sometimes that's good, but most of the time I prefer to be isolated from whatever else is playing in the house. I'm finding I reach for these more often when I'm in a quiet environment, and use ear buds when there's a lot of noise about (with me defining noise as any type of music I don't care for).

With the caveat of the lack of sound blocking, these should absolutely be on your short list if you're looking for a comfortable, great sounding pair of earphones.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones - Ivory

FDY MP3 Player, MP3 Player with Bluetooth5.0, 32GB Portable Music Player with FM Radio/Recorder, HiFi Lossless Sound Quality, 2.4Inch Touch Screen Mini MP3 Player for Running, Expandable 128GB TF When I opened the package containing this MP3 player, I was amazed at how small it is. But immediately became delighted at its perfectly small size. It is not the size of a small cellphone, but rather like what should have naturally occurred if an iPod shuffle mated with an iPod Nano. Perfect size and perfect function.

As the product description does not list or show the size of this MP3 player I list them here:

Length: 2 3/4 inches Width: 2 inches Thickness: 3/8 inch

Yes, small, but a powerhouse in functionality. I really miss the days when an MP3 player just played music. After a near fatal fall of my phone (luckily just the screen protector cracked!) it became important that an expensive phone might not be the best thing to lug around while performing yardwork. This excellent device solves that issue, and solves it well.

Songs and MP3 audio books were loaded easily onto the player. It is not made by Apple nor is part of their line, so the iTunes program does not work with this. However, it is a easy fix - just go to your Music folder on your computer, and drop the files you wish into this device's memory. Easy peasy and quick. It comes with an included 32 GB of memory, but can easily be upgraded if you install your own micro SD card, up to 128 GB.

It comes with wired earphones, which I did not use or test. With the invention of easy to pair Bluetooth earphones, I have no desire to be ever tethered with a headphone cord again. The player pairs easily with all 3 of my Bluetooth devices - earphones, headphones, and speakers. The sound from each device is flawless, which might be a function of the device, but is also determined by the source.

There are just 3 buttons on the side of this MP3 player - on/off button, volume up, and volume down. All other functions are controlled by the small but well designed touch screen. It is very comparable with the touch capability of modern phones, the programs are opened with ease and operate in an intuitive logical manner. There are other functions built into this device, but since I really got it as an MP3 player, that is what I am focused upon.

With this player comes a handy removable back clip, letting you clip it on/in a pocket, armband, belt, anywhere. Without the clip, it is small enough to easily slip into any pocked of your cloths, even the tiny change pockets in most jeans. Besides the wired earphones & clip, there is a 3mm audio cable for attaching it manually to another device, and a Micro USB cable for charging. There is a plastic protective film on the front face - it can be removed, but the touch screen operates just fine if it is left on.

This is my new favorite toy, It it not cheap or flimsy, but in all honesty, looks and feels like a tiny cell phone in how its constructed. It does not happen often, but this wonderful MP3 player exceeded my expectations.
text_fidelity_b: FDY MP3 Player, MP3 Player with Bluetooth5.0, 32GB Portable Music Player with FM Radio/Recorder, HiFi Lossless Sound Quality, 2.4Inch Touch Screen Mini MP3 Player for Running, Expandable 128GB TF

text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser PXC 450 Active Noise-Canceling Headphones I spend a great deal of time in a computer lab where there is literally over 1,000 running systems. In this environment, ear protection isn't absolutely necessary but without it there's some discomfort with which to deal because of all the fans in these systems and the requisite air handling units. I already have a pair of Bose QC-15 headphones but I am not a huge fan, so I recently purchased a pair of Sennheiser PXC-450 headphones for use in this environment. After an initial break-in period, I have come to really appreciate them.

This is going to be a comparative review, though primarily about the Sennheiser phones. Bose is generally regarded as the gold standard when it comes to ANC headphones, so matching the Sennheisers to the Bose is a good match-up. I'll break it all down into categories: Noise Canceling, Comfort, Sound Quality and Build Quality.

Noise Canceling:
Active noise canceling is THE primary feature of these phones and each has its strengths. Bose is, without question, the more capable ANC set when it comes to removing noise. This supremacy comes at a price though - because of the aggressiveness of their ANC, the wearer often feels a "pressure" on the ears when using the phones, something not present with the Sennheiser set which is close to Bose's level of canceling. Where Bose went to extremes to eliminate noise, Sennheiser went with the thought of "good enough for most". To be sure, both sets do a nice job of eliminating low frequency noise, enough to make air travel more pleasant if you dislike the rumble of plane engines.

They work in the car too (if you're not driving). I tried both sets in a moving vehicle and all do a fine job of eliminating road and engine noise. In fact, it was quiet to the point of eerie in the car. So, if you're a passenger on a long trip, either of these will work to suit your needs.

For the Sennheisers, you don't have to use ANC to listen to music as they provide the ability to override ANC and work like normal headphones. Bose, on the other hand, is an all-or-nothing deal and requires ANC to be on when listening to anything at all.

And that brings up a nice little feature on the Sennheisers - the "talk-thru" function, which allows a listener to cut off all sound and turn on a small microphone so that one can carry on a conversation without having to remove the headphones. No other headset I have ever used has this feature and it has already proven to be a handy tool.

Both sets require a single AAA battery to provide ANC. The battery life is definitely better with the Bose - mine last about a week between needing new batteries, whereas the Sennheiser set needs a new battery every other day.

Comfort:
The Sennheisers are the most comfortable headphones I have ever worn - period. The padding is buttery soft and they fit over my ears with no issue. Other reviewers have said that it seems like they just melt into your head, and that's a very accurate way to describe them. The Bose are nearly as comfortable, though they are slightly smaller.

Where the Sennheisers have a slight comfort disadvantage is actually in their size. These are big headphones and when they are worn around the neck instead of on the ears, they tend to rub on the neck and sometimes (depending on what you're doing) they can get in the way. If you take them off, or don't wear them around your neck, there's nothing about which to complain.

Sound Quality:
Sennheiser has always had premium sound, and the PXC-450 headphones demonstrate why they are the champs when it comes to quality sound. Though not audiophile phones, the PXC-450 brings awesome sound quality even at low volumes, with very full midrange and decent bass. The Bose sound great, except that the bass is too rich and without an equalizer in the mix the bass is enough to give me a headache over extended periods.

Build Quality:
I have not had the Sennheiser set very long but so far I have had no trouble with them. They feel rugged and sturdy, though they are mostly plastic so they do scratch and twist easily. The cord is heavy gauge wire, a welcome improvement over the cabling on Sennheiser sets I have worn in the past. The Bose set is a little more flimsy, with lesser gauge wire.

In summary, I find that the Sennheiser PXC-450 headphones are a better product than the Bose QC-15 headphones. They sound great, feel comfortable and they do a fine job of canceling noise. Bose does have better ANC and if that is the main thing you need and you don't mind the sensation of pressure they put on the ears then Bose is a better choice, but in almost every other aspect the Sennheisers bring more to the table.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser PXC 450 Active Noise-Canceling Headphones

text_fidelity_a:
Tascam TH-02 Closed Back Studio Headphones, Black [Great Sound]

As noted in some of the other reviews this pair of headphones has great sound for its price range. Sound is quite neutral, without the bass emphasis of a lot of headphones at this range. Highs are also good and not muted. The cable is also very generous in length, which is great as my computer is far away from my chair. Finally, the headband adjustment is exceptional. I have a fairly large skull and most headphones I've purchased have not fit well. However, this one fits perfectly and even has more room to expand. The only comfort downside is that the pads have quite a stiff covering material. This is not so great for comfort for long use sessions, but not too big of an issue as you can replace them eventually if needed. The thicker pad material would make the headphones last longer...if it were not for the major issue I describe below with build quality.

[Disappointing Build Quality]

I've had my pair for about 1.5 years now, and today the headphone snapped at the joint between the top band and where the extension band slides out. See attached photo. You can see that there is a metal band in the headband to provide elasticity and resistance. But the extension band (the part that slides in and out) doesn't have a metal band inside of it. This concentrates stress at this transition point, causing the plastic to snap here eventually. I noticed that the plastic on the other cup has also started cracking. The plastic itself feels quite brittle and is about as thick as the metal strip in the headband. I think the fact that I have a large head and had to extend the headphones out only hastened their demise as this put more stress on the plastic-only part of the headbands.

[Conclusion]

This is a great sounding pair of headphones for their price, but alas I cannot recommend them anymore due to the snapping of the headband. To fail after about a year of use is a bit on the low end. My previous pair of similarly priced headphones lasted over 10 years without the headband failing (only cable had become worn). I think you *might* be OK if you have a smaller head and don't have to extend the headphone band too much, but if you have to expand it to near its maximum, it will probably snap off like mine did.
text_fidelity_b: Tascam TH-02 Closed Back Studio Headphones, Black
