JLab Rewind Wireless Retro Headphones | Bluetooth 4.2 | 12 Hours Playtime | Custom EQ3 Sound | Music Controls | Noise Isolation | with Microphone | Throwback 80s 90s Design | Black I wasn't expecting much given the price of this item, and I got pretty much what I expected.

The charging port is hard to reach and the LED charging indicator is difficult, if not impossible to see, without having to move the foam earpiece covering.

Setting up/pairing the device is pretty easy. Press the button for 4 seconds or so and you’ll hear a pleasant female voice say, “Hello”. This means the power is on. Continue holding the button and the device will enter pairing mode. You’ll hear the voice say, “Ready to pair.” When pairing is complete, you’ll hear the device say, “You’re connected” and tell you how much charge the battery has. So far, all I’ve heard is, “Battery full.” I have no idea what other battery indications the voice will give – perhaps only at 3/4, 1/2 and 1/4? Or maybe percentages?

The buttons are the biggest drawback with this device. Actually, it's really just one multi-function button on the right earpiece. The button functionality is not like any Bluetooth headset I've used before - very non-intuitive. The button has no label at all and the tactile feedback is nonexistent at times - I press the button sometimes and there's no "click" feeling. If a song is playing, it doesn't seem to matter where I press, the song stops if it is playing. When I press again, anywhere, it starts playing again.

There is no volume control on the headphones at all. You’ll have to adjust the volume from your phone/audio player. There is a bare bones EQ function. You control this by clicking the multi-function button 3 times in rapid succession. Each time you do this, the device advances to the next of 3 EQ setting – balanced, bass boost and JLab signature. The “balanced” setting seems to sound just like what it’s named – balanced or equal high, mid and low tones. The bass boos is decent – not overbearing. Not sure what the last one is, but if the pictograms in the manual are any indication, it boost the high and low ends. The EQ function does provide audible feedback – the voice announces each setting by name.

There's a next track function, but no function for going to the previous track. The next track function requires holding down the multi-function button for 2 seconds. There's no audible feedback for this function (other than a very short moment of silence). When you hear the silence, let go IMMEDIATELY. If you hold the button down for too long the Bluetooth connection will be severed and you'll have to reconnect.

Apparently, there's no ability to fast forward or rewind within a song or audio book. You'll have to do this on your phone/audio player. Pretty poor design if you ask me. BTW – I use this only with my audio player, so I did not test the phone/mic functions, but I’d be surprised if they were robust.

The instructions are minimal at best. The manual is one piece of paper printed on 2 sides. Unfolded, it's about the size of 2 business cards - about 4"x4.5" (10.16cm x 11.43cm). One side has instructions and the other is all promotions/disclaimers, etc. That's it.

Sound quality is acceptable - decent bass and stereo separation is good. I’m no audiophile though. The product description says it has "Noise Isolation", which is marketing speak used by all on-ear headphone manufacturers. It simply means the ambient noise is slightly reduced because the headphones cover your ears. Bottom line - there's no tech/function in this device that does any active noise cancellation.

The headphones are a little snug/tight, but not so much to be uncomfortable - at least that's my opinion after an hour+ of testing. Not sure if this will be true for something like a 3-4 hour flight. I’ll test this out in the near future and will update this review, if possible.

The charging cable that comes with the item is 9” long (22.86cm). Not very useful at all, but better than nothing.

On the plus side, the manufacturer did provide an extra set of foam earpiece covers - the set that comes on the headphones is orange. The extra set is black.

Bottom line, for $15 I wasn't expecting a lot - well maybe better button functionality, but hey, what can you do? As my granddad used to say, “You pays your money and you takes your chances.”
text_fidelity_b: JLab Rewind Wireless Retro Headphones | Bluetooth 4.2 | 12 Hours Playtime | Custom EQ3 Sound | Music Controls | Noise Isolation | with Microphone | Throwback 80s 90s Design | Black

The fact that this unit has a built in Ethernet port is what led me to wanting this WiFi extender - the smart TV which is farthest from the primary router has had difficulty maintaining a solid connection so I wanted to utilize the Ethernet port on this extender to plug my TV directly into.

Set up of the extender was fairly straightforward, I plugged it into a power supply and ran an Ethernet cable from it to my laptop. The NETGEAR EXTENDER setup program auto loaded and was easy to follow. I setup the router to keep my same network name and password, it saved all of the information to my extender without issue. I unplugged the extender from both the power supply and my computer and located it into the bedroom, plugged it in and it found and connected to my WiFi without any issue. I plugged the smart TV into the Ethernet port and it connected beautifully - loading Netflix, HULU and Amazon Prime lightning fast.

The only hiccup happened when I finished that as the rest of my network went haywire with my smart devices not connecting and reconnecting. I restarted my modem and my primary router and everything appears to be back to operating as normal. I’m not sure what caused the glitch.

I can definitely see a WiFi speed increase in the area of the house that the extender is located and the TV that is plugged into the Ethernet port is streaming perfectly.

I am very pleased with this extender and would recommend it to anyone who needed to extend their WiFi range or provide an Ethernet Port to a device that is too far from their current hub.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR WiFi Mesh Range Extender EX6400 - Coverage up to 2100 sq.ft. and 35 devices with AC1900 Dual Band Wireless Signal Booster & Repeater (up to 1900Mbps speed), plus Mesh Smart Roaming

text_fidelity_a:
Outdoor WiFi Security Camera, HD 1080P Wireless Survenience IP Camera with 32GB SD Card, IP66 Waterproof Bullet Camera for Home, Support Motion Detection FTP 65ft Night Vision Remote View Onvif Cam I selected this camera to mount on my front porch, with the intention of keeping a watchful eye on the front of the house. I was very skeptical of this camera because of the price and assumed that it would be a budget-grade solution as a result. It has proven to be better than I anticipated.

This is a single-camera solution with no dedicated monitoring station. It connects via the WiFi network and it can be monitored via phone which is handy when you’re away. It includes a power supply and all of the mounting equipment (minus the tools) to set it all up for outdoor use.

All of that sounds great, but as I write this the camera sells for under $40.

It has not performed like a $40 camera. It has been rock-solid so far – it’s stable, it has remained connected except for when I have had router issues, the image in the daytime is excellent and the night-vision mode is far and away better than I expected – I can read license plates on cars in the driveway at night.

This is not a complete security solution but rather is a single camera for zone security. There are more complete systems that offer more features and capabilities, but these cost a lot more and cover broader areas with multiple cameras. If you just need a single camera to monitor a fairly small area, and you have a wireless network to connect it to, this is a very affordable solution.
text_fidelity_b: Outdoor WiFi Security Camera, HD 1080P Wireless Survenience IP Camera with 32GB SD Card, IP66 Waterproof Bullet Camera for Home, Support Motion Detection FTP 65ft Night Vision Remote View Onvif Cam

CTVISION 4K 8MP Home Business Wired Security Camera Systems,8-Channel 4K 8MP PoE Network Video Recorder(4TB HDD),8pc 4K (4X1080P) Outdoor Dome PoE IP Camera,Free App,P2P Cloud,Onvif,Video Surveillance [[VIDEOID:5b880a1d8f11ab783ee7340a330164be]] I ordered the ‘CTVISION 4K 8MP Home Business Wired Security Camera Systems,8-Channel 4K 8MP PoE Network Video Recorder(4TB HDD),8pc 4K (4X1080P) Outdoor Dome PoE IP Camera,Free App,P2P Cloud,Onvif,Video Surveillance’ for review and would like to share my thoughts.

I will lay this out as pros and cons and give some final thoughts.

Pros: The kit as a whole is well made.
Cameras are well made.
The 4tb hard drive is a good name brand and seems to be performing quite well.
The video quality is good.
The kit comes with 8X good quality 50 foot CAT5 cables (more on this in the cons)

Cons: The included cables are only 50 feet each. In a home install, if you are trying to run cameras to all corners of your house, 50 feet is not long enough in my case. I only used three of these cables. I had to buy more cable (CAT6) for the longer runs.
Although the cameras are well made, because they are of the Dome type, if you adjust the cameras to point at much of an angle, you run into issues at night when the IR lights turn on. This causes the IR lights to reflect back at the cameras (See attached video) The best angle for the cameras are to point straight down or at a very slight angle.
Speaking of angles, these cameras only have a 90 degree diagonal viewing angle which was a little disappointing.
When viewing the live feed, sometimes the video feed gets distorted for a couple of seconds.
The software of the NVR is a little overwhelming and hard to navigate. This is probably due to the fact that I have never used this type of system before. There are a lot of options in the Software which does not work with these specific cameras, such as Human Detection or PTZ (Pan Tilt Zoom). Not having the PTZ is really no big deal but it would have been nice to have the Human Detection so that the cameras don’t alarm when the wind blows the trees and shrubs.
There is an option to send an email when there is motion detected on the cameras but I was never able to get that to work.
Although there is an email option, I would have liked to see a text option.

Overall I am actually happy with this kit. It at least provides peace-of-mind knowing that the cameras are always recording and with the included 4tb hard drive in this kit, it provides many hours of footage. I hope that this was somewhat helpful.
text_fidelity_b: CTVISION 4K 8MP Home Business Wired Security Camera Systems,8-Channel 4K 8MP PoE Network Video Recorder(4TB HDD),8pc 4K (4X1080P) Outdoor Dome PoE IP Camera,Free App,P2P Cloud,Onvif,Video Surveillance

To me, the brand doesn’t matter – I do try to keep my equipment the same, but the Logitech ones have never let me down. They’re also better shaped for my hand, though the ones of the last decade are smaller, which I LOVE. Last year when I got a new laptop for my birthday, I got the new little Logi listed above.

I saw another HP mouse on here, the HP 930 Creator, and though that would be awesome. It wasn’t. I was quite disappointed. Not that I didn’t like my Logi, I though the HP would be a bit better. And, the 930 was over $67. Many problems, but the main one – size. Far too big for me in height and width.

I saw this and thought it might be better than the 930 – was certainly simpler. I love the FLAT design. It’s about half the height of my Logi.

This, like the 930 has a width problem, thus small hands and those with dexterity issues will have some problems “getting a grip”.

Another issue with this – you need BLUETOOTH capabilities.

Function?

Connection: After turning on my computer’s BLUETOOTH, the mouse connected in under 5 minutes

Sound: A bit quieter than my Logi, as well as the 930 Creator

Scroll: A bit slower than the Logi, definitely slower than the 930

Battery Replacement: Logi – on the bottom, like usual; 930 (rechargeable through USB). This? The battery is on the TOP. You have to remove the top black plate to put the battery in. This is the feature I dislike the most considering how THIN the plastic piece is. Depending on the amount of force used – it could easily get broken.

Currently priced at $39.76, this is definitely a bit overpriced. I am not fond of it, and definitely wouldn’t get a replacement.

UPDATE: As of 3/26, the mouse keeps losing Bluetooth connectivity sometimes in as little as 15 minutes of non-use. I don't know if this is normal with the Bluetooth mouse, but it is definitely annoying especially when I have to reconnect.
text_fidelity_b: HP 410 Slim Bluetooth Mouse - Bluetooth 5.0, Swift Pair, Blue optical sensor, adjustable up to 1600 DPI tracking, Portable, sleek for Wins PC, Laptop, Notebook, Mac, Work with Chromebook (4M0X5AA#ABL)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony Smart Control with Smartphone App and Simple All in One Remote - Black Build and Setup:
This is a very solid remote. Well constructed. It takes a disk watch type battery that is activated when you remove the tab. The lines are clean and elegant, and it feels well constructed.

Set up was very simple. I simply logged into myharmony.com and choose the Add a remote option.

The difference between this remote and other Harmony remotes is that this has a hub and blaster units that connects through your wireless network to allow you to connect and control your units with your smartphone.

You have to connect the hub and blaster unit around the units you want to control. It has to be connected to your home wireless network, which was easy. You can either do it through myharmony.com or by pressing the setup button on the hub and your router (if it supports it) it was that easy.

This particular unit controls my TV, Dish DVR, and VCR/DVD combo. Setting it up for the units was quite easy.

Using the Remote:
One selling point this has over the Ultimate is that the number buttons are solid state buttons, unlike the touch screen buttons on the Ultimate. As much as I like the touch screen technology, having buttons you can press by touch is a plus for.

There are also traditional DVR buttons, fast forward, as well as red, blue yellow, and green buttons. Since this remote did not have a 30 second advance button, and I rely on that, I programmed a short press of the green and yellow buttons to act as the skip forward. I programmed long pressing those buttons to do the default actions of those buttons. I appreciated that you could customize in that way.

Phone App:
The phone app for the android is a bit lacking as it is not quite as sophisticated as the remote itself, but can do most of the actions of the remote as long as you are connected to the same wireless network as your hub is.

Troubleshooting:
The remote is easy to use and troubleshoot, Simply rebooting or re-syncing the remote can resolve most problems I've found. It also prompts you for assistance the first time you add an action or new device.

Overall this is a great remote. This will demand, though, some knowledge on your part as it is a very sophisticated remote. Many problems that occur can easily be resolved by some knowledge of networks, remotes, or Harmony devices in general. If you have experience with this you will enjoy the functions and capacity of this remote.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony Smart Control with Smartphone App and Simple All in One Remote - Black

Fire TV Stick streaming device with Alexa built in, includes Alexa Voice Remote, HD, latest release I have the original fire stick and I love it. I have 2 TVs, 1 in my living room and 1 in my bedroom. Because I love the original fire stick (gift from my son ❤) I finally decided to get a 2nd for my bedroom. I bought this upgraded fire stick on Prime Day. I got it yesterday. I'm amazed that the remote can link to my TV and control the TV. I read from other reviewers that it powers on their TV. If this is true, then I will be ecstatic. My TV remote is HUGE and I hate it. The TV was built in 2006 so the TV and remote are huge. Both work great. I was originally going to just use my Chromecast as I love the casting from room to room without losing my place. However, since the fire stick remote controls the TV I am rethinking my thoughts. I was amazed that the fire stick was soooooo easy to set up. It recognized my Wi-Fi ID and my password for the WI-FI. I did not need to give the code. I think that it picked up all the information that the original fire stick has, including Wi-Fi information. This makes the upgraded fire stick the easiest set up ever. I also noticed that the speed of the processor is incredible. Not once have I noticed any buffering. I do get buffering from my other 3 devices. Guess it's time to replace my original fire stick with this one. This fire stick replaced my Roku which I've had for years and still works fine. The reason why I replace the Roku was that Roku seems to be incompatible with Hulu Live (love it BTW). It keeps shutting off the program that i am watching making me yo go back into my Hulu account again. Just imagine, you're watching a show and just at the most interesting part, it flicks and goes back to the home screen. Ahhhhh!!!! Since this fire stick performs so well, I'm thinking of not even using my 2 Chromecasts anymore. Now that's progress! The 2 Chromecasts do have some lagging and that's why I'm thinking of just using the fire stick and buying a new one for the living room. If anyone was on the fence about buying this fire stick, don't be. This purchase was well worth the money. Go for it!! I was going to upgrade my internet because I thought the lagging was them, nope. This fire stick has out performed my wildest dreams. Go buy this, fire stick you won't be sorry!! Oh one last thing, I've noticed that some reviewers have complained about opening up the battery case. It's actually easy, you simply press dojwn on the circle at the top and push the cover to the opposite side. You will hear a little pop. That's releasing the lock. Then you will see a small space where the circle is, just stick your fingernail (presuming your nail is not so bitten to the point where it's below the nail line) and push. Easy peasy! Amazon clearly have their products hooked up! I love the ease of Amazon, hands down. ❤. If my opinion changes about the upgraded fire stick, I'll post an update.

UPDATE: Its very easy to navigate the fire stick but if you can't find something all you have to do is ask Alexa and she will find it for you. It also fully takes charge of your TV. There is nothing you need With the original clunky remote. Unless you want to access your HDMI ports. But with all that the fire stick offers, you don't need another dongle. I will be using the fire stick only. It's so wonderful to use one small, comprehensive remote. Basically Amazon has updated the fire stick to make it a universal remote. Now I'm going to buy a remote cover so I can easily see my new "universal" remote in the dark. ❤😎

I purchased a second Fire Stick from a big box store. I'm sorry that I did. When you buy a Fire Stick through Amazon, they load it with your account information making set up super easy. When you buy one through the box box stores they are generic and set up was a bit more difficult. Suggestion folks but your Fire Stick through Amazon and forget the big box stores! Wish I would have known this before I purchased my second one! Never again!!

The screen swivels around so you can fold this in half "backwards" so only the screen is showing. This is helpful when using the case for use in a vehicle.

Compared to my regular TV this is an enhanced viewing experience. I found this to be a better visual experience. All the colors were vivid and almost velvety. Whether I am watching a favorite movie or a nature DVD, the colors are fantastic. Greens and yellows are super crisp and water looks totally glossy. I can't emphasize enough how beautiful the colors are on the screen.

I found many uses for this DVD player. It literally became my entertainment companion for two days while I tried out every feature. What I loved best was playing my virtual fireplace DVD with a beach fire and ocean waves. The stereo sound on this is excellent, I felt I was really at the beach which made me happy.

The remote control works very well and allows you to do things like turn the subtitles on or off. The audio controls let you choose between various options. You can stop or pause the movie you are watching either from the controls on the DVD player or by using the remote control.

This DVD player also has a screen saver that comes up when you put it on pause or don't turn the screen off. There is a button that says TFT ON/OFF that turns the screen off when you only want to listen to the sound. I found this played CDs too so that made me very happy. You can listen with the stereo speakers or use headphones.

If you are looking to view widescreen movies, this works for that too.

This is perfect to take with you when traveling. The only caution is not to use it for yourself if you are driving. It does have a cigarette charger that will work in cars and RVs.

The only thing I do when taking out a CD or DVD is to turn the DVD player off completely.

Some other uses I found for this DVD player was to play relaxing DVDs before bed to calm the mind. I also watched an underwater DVD with fish swimming by. This DVD player allows you to have entertainment wherever you are. The battery lasts about 4-5 hours, but if it starts to run out you can just plug the unit in and continue watching.

The only thing I noticed that was different than a regular DVD player was when you are halfway through a movie, put it on pause instead of taking out the DVD. This does not seem to have any memory of where you left off so when you put the DVD back in it just starts from the beginning again. This is not a big issue if you just hit the pause button.

I'm very happy with this DVD player and it is fun to go into your own little movie world. This is handy to have when someone else is using the computer or main TV. You can watch movies anywhere you want. I use this mostly when sitting in bed.

text_fidelity_a:
Monoprice Blackbird 4K 3x1 HDMI 1.4 Switch - Compact, HDCP 2.2, Built-in Equalizer, 4K 30Hz, YCbCr 4:4:4, 18Gbps (Compatible with PS4/5 Xbox Apple TV Fire Stick Roku Blu-Ray Player) Since we mounted our TV we like to use as few chords as possible. This way they are neatly tucked along the wall and down into the entertainment center where all our entertainment equipment is housed. So the main HDMI cable runs down but of course we have more components that require a cable than the one connected to the TV. Our solution? A signal splitter. Thankfully, we have only three output connections so this one seemed perfect. Plus, it touts 4k signal, even though most pre-4k HDMI boxes should be fine, but it's nice to have that in the title just in case.

What I use this mostly for is the cable box and a couple of video game systems. As for the cable box, seems to work fine; no dropped signals that I've noticed, nor any degradation in quality. As for game consoles, I have the PS3 and the Wii U hooked up to it. SAme: no noticeable quality degradation nor input lag.
Now, to put it to the real test, I hooked up some retro consoles that have been modded to output native HDMI; that means they'll be HDMI with no lag. Considering I have this and two HDMI cables connecting the console to the TV, I was curious to see if there truly was any lag.
With older games, timing is everything, especially on the 8-bit consoles with platformers and fighters, like the NES. From what I could tell, there was absolutely no lag, not to mention signal loss. The buttons responded as though I were using a normal NES on a CRT.

So yeah, I'm pretty satisfied. It's a bit light and doesn't have heavy pads on the bottom to prevent it from sliding around. With so many cables, and the ability to use the remote control, it should be a bit more stable on the surface.
I haven't used the remote as the detections are instant. No need to manually switch the inputs, at least from my experience. Also, I didn't need to use the power adapter; the power from the HDMI cables seemed to be sufficient, and the detection was not complicated by the lack of adapter. Weird.
text_fidelity_b: Monoprice Blackbird 4K 3x1 HDMI 1.4 Switch - Compact, HDCP 2.2, Built-in Equalizer, 4K 30Hz, YCbCr 4:4:4, 18Gbps (Compatible with PS4/5 Xbox Apple TV Fire Stick Roku Blu-Ray Player)

I think it is perfect for the average student (high school or college) or for the home. Set-up is really easy. It is lightweight and fits into the average laptop bag. The sound quality from the built-in speakers is decent, so listening to videos or music is great. There is also one feature of this computer that I really like. It has fingerprint technology which adds an extra layer of security. Now, the two things that I would change about this computer: additional memory and make it a touch screen.  First, why not have more memory out of the box versus having to add some later. AND don’t most screens today come with touch technology? I think that would be an awesome feature.  However, for the cost, this computer has a decent amount of bang for the buck. It is affordable, lightweight and can do a lot, especially for students. And since my son will be entering his freshman year this fall, I will probably let him take this laptop.

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin Nuvi 2595LMT UPDATE: after installing the latest map update and waiting for a very long time for the install software to do its thing and worrying if it had actually finished the install because after about an hour my computer said "the application has unexpectedly quit," the device seems to be working perfectly.

Overall, I like the 2595LMT. It boots and finds the satellites faster and has more information available.

Pros:
1. I can press the lower left "Arrive time" button and change it to a variety of readouts: miles remaining, altitude, time via.
2. Voice command works, mostly, especially on simple commands like "Go Home." More complex commands, like an address, return a wide variety of responses, most of them wrong. (Why it's searching the entire United States when it knows where I am and should be looking locally is beyond me.) I liked the old way of narrowing search to State, then City, then Address. Now it just asks you for the whole address, which it likely doesn't understand.
3. It's slimmer and lighter.
4. Easy to import my favorites from my old Nuvi into the 2595LMT. Using a PC, after plugging the old Nuvi into a computer using the USB port,

a. Navigate until you find the "current.GPX" file on the old Nuvi and
b. Copy it to your desktop (this is also a way to make a backup should you desire.)
c. Rename the file: replace "current" with any word you want, as long as it's not "current") so that it is names "anyword.gpx"
d. Attach the new Nuvi 2595LMT to the computer and navigate until you find the folder with its "current.gpx" file.
e. Copy the "anyword.gpx" file from the desktop into the same folder where the "Current.gpx" file resides.
f. Disconnect and restart. All the old favorites will be added to the current list in your new Nuvi.

5. It doesn't say "recalculating" when you disregard its directions
6. It has lane indicators: a series of arrows in the upper left that tell you which lane to get into to make the next turn. Very cool.
7. Touch screen allows scrolling like a smartphone, at least on some screens.
8. Allows you to add/edit shortcuts like a PC. You can create and move icons around so that you can get to a particular feature with one touch.
9. Micro-SD card only
10. Bigger screen
11. 3-D view of the road
12. Speed limit indicator and simultaneous readout of your actual speed that turns red if you exceed the local speed limit. (I wish it bonged quietly when the speed limit changed to remind you that you have to go slower or can go faster.)

Cons:
1. Sadly, on my unit (even after map and software updates) when I say, "Find Place" it immediately crashes and reboots. And if I say, "Find City" it ignores me, even if I ask it to find New York or Los Angeles. I may try reinstalling the software in case it loaded incompletely for some reason. (UPDATE: I waited a couple of weeks and tried updating the maps again. This time it fully installed and happily all the voice commands now work very well. This alone is a good reason to get is unit. Typing while driving is difficult and dangerous. Voice command is simply wonderful and something I've always wanted in a Garmin.)
2. Stuff has been moved around so that the interface is a bit foreign. For instance, "Favorites" are now "Saved Places" and trying to save or edit a saved place is confusing until you get the hang of it.
3. Doesn't have a powered cradle anymore, only a standard mini-USB on the back. Not a real problem, but it's slower to hook up and remove. I used to be able to drop it on the cradle and go. Now I have to find the end of the cable and thread it into a small port on the back. Minor.
4. The traffic function in my opinion is a joke. Driving LA freeways at most times involves congestion and some delay. It's simply the way it is. The Garmin hates congestion and is constantly trying to get you around it. Thus it's constantly bonging and telling me to get off the freeway to take surface streets, assuming they are magically uncongested when in reality the surface streets during rush hour are ten times worse. I'm pretty much going to ignore its traffic suggestions and may turn it off altogether. If you buy the amazon basics power cord [[ASIN:B003N2POXK AmazonBasics Vehicle Power Cable with Mini-USB Connector for GPS and Other Mini-USB Devices]] it doesn't have a built in traffic receiver and thus defeats the annoying and constant attempts to route you around congestion. Simply put, don't believe the alternate route is going to save you any time. Getting onto surface streets during rush hour is a recipe for even longer delays.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin Nuvi 2595LMT

SanDisk Cruzer Fit CZ33 32GB USB 2.0 Low-Profile Flash Drive- SDCZ33-032G-B35 Capacity is more than adequate for my needs, and the price is right. But the real reason why I gave it five stars is this drive is absolutely reliable. I have tried other brands only to experience premature death of the drive, data loss and other frustrations. In fact, one would get so hot in large transfers that it was uncomfortable to touch. This one does not have those flaws.

I use a pair of these. One for backing up my documents on my ThinkPad T61 running Win XP, and the other as a portable music library. For the latter use I've plugged it into my Galaxy Note 3 phone and Samsung tablet via a [[ASIN:B00C7SK2J2 Micro USB OTG Host Cable to USB 2.0 Adapter]], as well as a number of PCs and laptops of fellow musicians.

Just about every operating system, from my Android phone to a friend's Win 8 laptop immediately recognized this as a drive as soon as it was inserted in the USB port.

I did not bother measuring the transfer speed because I mostly use this for streaming music via USB. I have never experienced a freeze or lag in playing, so, again, I am very pleased with it. The final reason why I am happy is the small form factor, which is about the size of a bluetooth dongle.

Bottom line is you can save a few bucks by purchasing a competing brand, but you will get what you pay for in my opinion. I've been using this brand for literally decades and have never had to worry about failure or other issues.
